revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule limits a constant function call to a constant function local to the calling module or from a package or $unit; it does not include the 2023 static-class-function and calling-design-element formulation.

The 2017 rule limits a constant function call to a constant function local to the calling module or from a package or $unit; it does not include the 2023 rule for static class functions, including parameterized static class functions, local to a calling design element.

The 2012 rule requires an invoked constant function to be local to the current module and separately permits only system functions allowed in constant expressions; it lacks the 2023 exception for all built-in methods on function-local variables.

The 2017 rule requires an invoked function to be a constant function local to the current module and separately permits only system functions allowed in constant expressions; it lacks the 2023 exception permitting all built-in methods on local variables.
The 2012 rule imposes definition-before-call ordering on parameter values, but does not include the 2023 rule's explicit coverage of type parameters.
The 2017 rule requires parameter values used by the function to be defined before the invoking call; the 2023 rule explicitly extends this ordering requirement to both value and type parameters.
The 2012 rule ignores all system task calls in a constant function; it does not provide the 2023 exception for elaboration severity system tasks.
The 2017 rule ignores all system task calls in a constant function; it does not provide the 2023 exception that executes elaboration severity system tasks.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic_override_specifiers construct on function declarations.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no dynamic override specifiers on function declarations.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic_override_specifiers construct on task declarations.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no dynamic override specifiers on task declarations.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define a nonvoid function call as an implicit variable supporting member selection or indexing.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define a nonvoid function call as an implicit variable of its return type for member selection or indexing.
IEEE 1800-2012 lacks the function-call-as-implicit-variable construct and therefore has no associated mandatory-parentheses rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 lacks the function-call-as-implicit-variable construct and therefore has no associated mandatory-parentheses rule.

IEEE 1800-2012 defines input defaulting and inheritance of an explicit direction, including const ref, but its ref-direction grammar has no static qualifier and therefore lacks the 2023 static-ref inheritance guarantee.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines input as the initial default and inheritance of an explicit direction, but does not include the 2023 inheritance rule for const and static qualifiers on ref.

The 2012 text permits fine-grain process-control methods to suspend the current or another process, but does not state the 2023-specific permission to kill the current process or kill, suspend, or resume another process.

IEEE 1800-2017 permits fine-grain process control methods to suspend the current or another process; the 2023 rule instead enumerates killing, suspending, or resuming another process and killing the current process.
IEEE 1800-2012 forbids every ref argument in contexts forbidden for automatic variables and has no ref static exception.
IEEE 1800-2017 prohibits ref arguments in contexts forbidden for automatic variables without the 2023 ref static exception.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no ref static formal-argument construct or its static-actual lifetime restrictions.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define ref static formals or their static-lifetime actual restrictions.
IEEE 1800-2012 provides direction inheritance including const ref, but has no static qualifier on ref formals and therefore no static-ref qualifier inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2017 makes subsequent undirected formals inherit the prior direction, but does not include the 2023 inheritance of const and static qualifiers on ref.
